newsitem.title: USA: IMF to send mission to Kabila's Congo.
newsitem.headline: IMF to send mission to Kabila's Congo.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund will send a mission to the Democratic Republic of the Congo next week for its first contacts with the administration of Laurent Kabila, a senior IMF official said on Thursday.

Evangelos Calamitsis, director of the IMF's Africa department, told Reuters that the mission would give IMF officials a chance to meet Kinshasa officials and see what sort of assistance could be on offer.
He said he hoped the former Zaire would draw on the reformist experiences of neighboring Uganda in assessing its economic policy priorities.

"I hope that the new Zaire -- I'll call it that to avoid confusion with the other Congo -- will look at the experience of Uganda and see what lessons it can draw from that experience," Calamitsis said.

"The new Zaire has had a lot of problems in the past, but it is obvious that they have to bring inflation under control, restore financial discipline and stamp out corruption. They have to restart a lot of their institutions, like the central bank."

Calamitsis said early assistance to Kinshasa would probably be technical becuase the IMF and Kinshasa needed to work out what to do about big debts to the IMF built up by the administration of ousted president Mobuto Sese Seko before loans were offered.
The country has had no reform program with the IMF since the 1980s, Calamitsis said.
